text:
alice.support: Heads-up — customer (AcmePay) opened a ticket: sudden change in outputs + some 400s after what looks like a region reroute. They see garbled tokens and function-calling failures. Correlation: cid=acme-req-9f2a, account=acmepay-prod.

ben.engineer: Can you paste the failing request/response? which region did the call land in?

alice.support: Sample from their logs (redacted):
```
POST /v1/generate \nHost: api.redwood.ai \nAuthorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx \n{
  "model": "redwood/gptj-13b",
  "input": "Summarize transaction 0xabc...",
  "functions": [{"name":"create_invoice","parameters":{"type":"object"}}],
  "request_id": "acme-req-9f2a"
}

Response: 400 {
  "error": "tokenizer_mismatch",
  "detail": "unknown token ids in response: [50257, 50258]",
  "served_model": "redwood/gptj-13b-lite-q4v2"
}
```

alice.support: They say this started at ~2026-03-15T14:02:03Z, after a nearshore probe. Traffic shows client region APAC but routing to nearshore standby (nearshore-us-central) for latency.

cameron.ml: That served_model is a lighter quantized variant with a different tokenizer config (weird but possible if variants were onboarded with per-variant vocab offsets). Tokenizer drift explains unknown token ids and broken function-calling / structured output.

ben.engineer: Do we have a routing event/rollback around that time? any autoscaler or standby failover?

deploy-bot: route-change: probe=nearshore-standby activated at 2026-03-15T14:01:50Z | policy=latency-fallback | session=route-scan-7781

dana.ops: Autoscaler bumped standby pool for nearshore (scale up) at 14:01:48Z and mark-for-activation set. Fallback policy allowed serving with any compatible "family" variant.

eli.sre: TL;DR: routing selected a model variant family-compatible by architecture but tokenizer/config didn't match customer's pinned tokenizer expectation => token IDs misaligned. We should treat tokenizer config as non-compatible in routing policy.

ben.engineer: Repro steps for SRE/ML:
1) Use the customer's payload and request_id.
2) Simulate routing with policy "latency-fallback" to nearshore-standby pool.
3) Confirm runtime logs: which model binary loaded and which tokenizer config path used.

alice.support: Customer wants hotfix asap — they have production traffic. They mentioned billing spikes due to retries. Priority: P0.

cameron.ml: Quick mitigation: add a temporary routing rule to prefer exact model version (if account has pin), or prefer global stable pool. I can push a hot patch to routing policy to disallow variants with different tokenizer_version metadata.

ben.engineer: Also suggestion: respond with explicit 5xx/429 on incompatible-variant detection instead of serving unknown tokens, so client can retry against stable route.

dana.ops: Implementing an emergency rule: block nearshore-standby from serving for accounts with active function-calling until we confirm tokenizer alignment. Rolling now.

deploy-bot: policy-change: deny-standby-for-fn-calls rolled by dana.ops at 2026-03-15T14:12:05Z (change-id pc-9921).

eli.sre: Postmortem TODOs:
- Treat tokenizer_version as routing-invariant metadata.
- Add a runtime check that rejects requests if served tokenizer_version != request.tokenizer_version (if provided) or != model_catalog[tokenizer_version].
- Add telemetry on unexpected token ids during streaming to trigger early rejection.

alice.support: Customer asked for repro evidence before we close the ticket. Ben/Cameron, can you drop a short repro log snippet and recommended long-term fix for the PM?

ben.engineer: Repro log snippet (sanitized):
```
[14:01:52.123] route_decision: client_region=apac-east, chosen_pool=nearshore-standby, policy=latency-fallback
[14:01:52.456] serve.load_model: name=redwood/gptj-13b-lite-q4v2, tokenizer=/models/gptj-13b/tokenizer_variant_b.json
[14:01:52.789] request: request_id=acme-req-9f2a, model_meta.tokenizer_version=variant_b
[14:01:53.001] runtime: generated_tokens [50257,50262,...] -> decode_error: unknown_token_id
[14:01:53.005] response: 400 tokenizer_mismatch served_model=redwood/gptj-13b-lite-q4v2
```

cameron.ml: For PM write-up: enforce tokenizer_version equality in routing + catalog metadata. Also audit onboarding scripts to ensure quant/size variants inherit tokenizer from canonical model or explicitly declare mismatch.

dana.ops: I've notified Account Success. Setting follow-up window 48h, will revert if any regressions.

alice.support: Thanks all — I'll update the customer with the mitigation + ETA for a permanent fix. :thumbsup:

eli.sre: Next action: schedule a small rollout to ensure no other customers are affected, and add an alert on "tokenizer_mismatch" errors crossing 5/min for any account.

alice.support: Closing loop for now; will reopen if AcmePay sees new errors.
